author: Ifmyante
text:
Hi Hansma

Eaten bread is soon forgotten. It's only human nature that makes people
leave. Either they found that they could never be traders, or they found
 enough to be profitable and need us no more.

About posting trades: If I were to post trades, they'd be fabrications. I
 haven't felt like trading in months, so haven't taken any trades.

If I did take trades though, they'd be exact replicas of the trades I've
 taken in the past. They're fast easy money, so there's no need to do
anything differently.

To answer a number of PMs I got from people wanting to join the academy,
 let me say this: There is absolutely no guarantee that you will be a
super trader after taking the course. Although I have some truly amazing
 graduates, others are buying the tops of ranges and selling the
bottoms, allowing massive risks per trade, not using the tools we've
designed for them, as if they've never taken the course at all!

This too is human nature. If all my students were machines, I could
simply program them and leave them to it. But they're not. They have
their own individual demons they must overcome if they can begin to do
it right and keep doing so.

author: Sean9henry
text:
Hello Hans and aspiring fellow traders,

I have been through different trading classes, some free and some paid. I
 have also learned something out of some classes, at least when I
attended the class. I didn't become profitable after the class, but the
class sellers kept on offering additional and more advanced classes.

Most don't make money after taking the classes, but I have seen people
who honestly make money. So that is what kept me going forward. After
about 5 years in the market, looking at the chart almost everyday, not
saying reading the chart, that is IF's specialty, I can tell which
strategy makes money OVER TIME, and which won't. Of course there are
those boarder line strategies you have to have numbers to show if it
makes money. I honestly have been making some, but because after I have
made some, I become more risk tolerant and trade more aggressively by
betting bigger and taking more risky trades, I then give it back. This
is partial psychology and partial problem of using a variety of
strategies.

I can fairly say that IF's strategy works with my five years of
experience. By saying this I am not convincing you to pay for the class
or not to. Human nature determines that people to look for best return
on minimal to no "apparent" cost. So after people fully learned the
strategy and making money, they may shift their focus of life and not
visit this site any more, let alone keep on posting trades for no
return. Or their personal life doesn't allow that time commitment
anymore or any other reasons.

As I see it, IF has given the new people the most direct free approach
to be skillful (not saying profitable because of psychological barrier)
in trading, that is something very commendable! Try the internet, you
will see there are people selling indicator after indicators, among
those some make money in trading, and some don't. Some educators send
out free videos daily to say how many hundreds or thousands they make
that day in live trading, but from their occasional slips you find out
they are simulating. I suspect they record several and pick the winning
live videos to send out. Funny things is even from those videos I
learned quite a bit that helped me in trading.

If you are interested in seeing how the IF style trades work, please
visit my journal at
"readthemarket.com/~readthe3/index.php/forum/journals/2256-sean-s-journal#42927",
 I just started it and will try to put a trade out before it triggers
and then follow up to see how it turns out. I will track the overall win
 and loss based on my risk (R, can be any amount but needs to be a fixed
 % of account size between 0.5% and 2%). Keep in mind that this is
thoughts sharing not trade recommendations. To be fair to IF, I will
only put out the RTM style trades as best as I get it. Of course, if IF
doesn't mind, I can add a small amount of other traditional trading
style live trades that I look for and take with real money. I do this
because it helps me understand the human psychology behind the chart
better. I don't sell or preach anything. I just like this community that
 IF has built.

In order not to clog up IF's journal, maybe people can share in my
journal about their trading journey and experience, just for fun and for
 mutual enlightening.

Good luck!

Sean.

author: Kossack
text:
Hi If,

I think you theory about students "not being machines" was proven long
time ago with "The Turtles" experiment in stock trading. Where although
given strict step-by-step instructions how to trade profitably, by some
famous trader, majority of them was not able to follow it and really
trade profitably. Then the question WHY? comes to mind.

And the answer is rather simple, people have encoded in them various personality patterns and this is one of them.

So there are "procedure" people who have absolutely no problem following
 instructions and get things done and "options" people who just simply
cannot follow instructions and have to either create their own procedure
 or at least modify the one they have...which in trading with proven
system is rather fatal....On the other hand "procedure" folks have
terribly hard time creating procedures or they cannot create them at
all.. Just a small psychology lesson
